title: The tree in winter
hook: a bare tree in winter, and an eighteen-year-old who sees the spring that isn't there yet
tomorrow: before the monastery, what kind of servant was he?

segments.voice: Yesterday closed The Story of a Soul with the little way: small things, great love, trust like a child. Your line was the little way. Now a new book, and another Carmelite who loved small things.

Nobody posts the winter view. Gray sky, slush by the curb, trees that look like wire. It's the season most feeds skip. Long before Thérèse, a young man in France stops in front of a tree like that. It's winter. The tree has nothing on it, not one leaf. He's eighteen. Nothing about this tree is beautiful, and nothing about the moment looks important. But something happens while he stands there, and he'll still be talking about it as an old man.
screen: `THE VIEW NOBODY POSTS.` → `A TREE WITH NOTHING ON IT.` → `EIGHTEEN, STANDING THERE.`

segments.voice: This is Brother Lawrence, who became a lay brother in a Carmelite monastery. The book with his name on it, The Practice of the Presence of God, isn't one he sat down to write. It's mostly a visitor's notes of conversations with him, plus some of his letters. And the first conversation opens with the tree. Lawrence told his visitor that God did him a singular favor in his conversion, at eighteen. It was winter, and he saw a tree stripped of its leaves. He considered that in a little while the leaves would come back, and after them the flowers, and then the fruit. Nothing on the branch proved it. From that sight, he said, he received a high view of the providence and power of God that never left his soul. It set him loose from the world, and lit a love for God so strong that, more than forty years on, he couldn't tell whether it had grown since. Notice what he didn't get. No voice, no vision. Just a bare thing, looked at with hope. That's the whole book in small: God found in plain things, ordinary days, kitchens and errands. Here's one to tell a friend tonight: a spiritual classic starts with a man staring at a tree with no leaves.
screen: `A VISITOR'S NOTES.` · `STRIPPED OF ITS LEAVES.` · `LEAVES, FLOWERS, FRUIT TO COME.` · `NO VISION, JUST A TREE.` · then, large: `SPRING WILL COME.`

segments.voice: If there's a window near you, find a tree and look at its branches; if not, bring one to mind, or look at any plant in the room. Rest your eyes on the bare parts, the places where nothing is happening yet. Keep looking while the sit runs.
The tree in winter. A bare tree that showed a young man the spring he couldn't see yet.
Your line: spring will come. A bare branch isn't the same as a dead one. See you tomorrow.
